title: The Wonderful City of Oz, part 6
attribution: From The Wonderful Wizard of Oz by L. Frank Baum (1900), via Project Gutenberg, in reading order.
body: “What must I do?” asked the girl.
“Kill the Wicked Witch of the West,” answered Oz.
“But I cannot!” exclaimed Dorothy, greatly surprised.

“You killed the Witch of the East and you wear the silver shoes, which bear a powerful charm. There is now but one Wicked Witch left in all this land, and when you can tell me she is dead I will send you back to Kansas—but not before.”
The little girl began to weep, she was so much disappointed; and the eyes winked again and looked upon her anxiously, as if the Great Oz felt that she could help him if she would.

“I never killed anything, willingly,” she sobbed. “Even if I wanted to, how could I kill the Wicked Witch? If you, who are Great and Terrible, cannot kill her yourself, how do you expect me to do it?”

“I do not know,” said the Head; “but that is my answer, and until the Wicked Witch dies you will not see your uncle and aunt again. Remember that the Witch is Wicked—tremendously Wicked—and ought to be killed. Now go, and do not ask to see me again until you have done your task.”

Sorrowfully Dorothy left the Throne Room and went back where the Lion and the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman were waiting to hear what Oz had said to her. “There is no hope for me,” she said sadly, “for Oz will not send me home until I have killed the Wicked Witch of the West; and that I can never do.”
Her friends were sorry, but could do nothing to help her; so Dorothy went to her own room and lay down on the bed and cried herself to sleep.
The next morning the soldier with the green whiskers came to the Scarecrow and said:
“Come with me, for Oz has sent for you.”

So the Scarecrow followed him and was admitted into the great Throne Room, where he saw, sitting in the emerald throne, a most lovely Lady. She was dressed in green silk gauze and wore upon her flowing green locks a crown of jewels. Growing from her shoulders were wings, gorgeous in color and so light that they fluttered if the slightest breath of air reached them.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does Oz tell Dorothy she must do?
options: Kill the Wicked Witch of the West
Bring him the Golden Cap
Cross the great desert alone
Give up the silver shoes

questions.prompt: Per the passage, when will Oz send Dorothy back to Kansas?
options: When she can tell him the Witch is dead
As soon as she asks a second time
After she has stayed a year in the city
He refuses ever to do it

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did Dorothy do when she left the Throne Room?
options: Went to her room and cried herself to sleep
Set off for the West that same hour
Asked the soldier to take her back in
Told her friends she had succeeded

questions.prompt: Per the passage, who came for the Scarecrow the next morning?
options: The soldier with the green whiskers
The Guardian of the great Gates
The green girl with green hair
Dorothy and the Cowardly Lion

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what form did Oz take for the Scarecrow?
options: A most lovely Lady with wings
An enormous Head without a body
A terrible Beast with five eyes
A Ball of Fire that scorched

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what is Dorothy's objection to the task?
options: She has never willingly killed anything and cannot see how
She does not believe the Witch of the West exists
She has no way of travelling to the West
She has promised the Good Witch not to fight

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what argument does Dorothy turn back on Oz?
options: If he cannot kill the Witch himself, how can she?
If he is good, why does he ask for a killing?
If he is a wizard, why does he need her shoes?
If she kills the Witch, who will rule the Winkies?

That he never expected her to succeed
That the Witch cannot be killed at all
That he would rather she stayed in the city

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does sorrowfully describe about Dorothy's leaving?
options: She left full of grief
She left in a great hurry
She left without saying anything
She left more determined than before

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the passage?
options: The price of going home turns out to be a killing Dorothy cannot face
The Wizard agrees to send Dorothy home at once
Dorothy persuades the Wizard to ask for something easier

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did Oz say the silver shoes bear?
options: A powerful charm
The mark of the Witch of the East

Nothing of any use

questions.prompt: Per the passage, how many Wicked Witches are left in the land?
options: One
Two
Three
None

options: Green silk gauze and a crown of jewels
A green uniform and a long beard
Thick woolly hair over all her body

options: Anxiously, as if he hoped she could help him

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, how do her friends respond to Dorothy's news?
options: They are sorry but can do nothing to help

They urge her to go back and argue again
They decide to leave the city at once

How strong the wind in the room was
How frightened she was of the Scarecrow

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarises the passage?
options: A hard condition is set, and the Wizard changes shape for the next visitor
A wizard proves kinder to the Scarecrow than to Dorothy
